title: [CQ-I06d] JetBrains approval error correlation
description:
Objective: make the JetBrains plan review consume daemon ERROR frames the way VS Code's PlanReviewPanel.handleClientError does. Verified on 2026-10-30:
- MoeMessageDispatcher keeps only `message` and `operation` from an ERROR frame. It drops the frame's `codeName` and `context.taskId`.
- PlanReviewDialog.onError feeds EVERY error frame into PlanReviewApprovalState.onDaemonError, which re-arms a PENDING approval.

So any unrelated error that arrives while an approval is pending re-arms the dialog with a misleading 'The daemon refused the approval: <other text>'. Examples: another operation, another task, or a payload error with no context. When WORKING then arrives at the captured revision, it is reported as status-changed, never as approved. VS Code ignores uncorrelated frames, and latches on a correlated PLAN_REVISION_MISMATCH. CQ-I06 DoD 1 ('Both clients consume identical daemon verdicts') needs one behaviour.

Deliverable:
- The dispatcher strictly parses `codeName` and `context.taskId`: strings only, anything else becomes null.
- It publishes them through a NEW default MoeStateListener method, so the four existing onError(operation, message) implementers stay unchanged.
- The dialog reacts only to operation APPROVE_TASK whose context.taskId equals its task:
  - a correlated PLAN_REVISION_MISMATCH latches INVALIDATED with PLAN_CHANGED_KEY;
  - any other correlated error re-arms with DAEMON_ERROR_KEY, as today.
- Tests for each case.

Out of scope:
- the daemon frame shape, which already carries operation, code, codeName and context {taskId, epicId, revisions};
- VS Code, CLIENT_HELLO, and the shared verdict corpus (CQ-I06b);
- any other listener's error handling.

Verification (run fresh, exit 0 required): cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test. WSL has no JDK, so run the Windows gradlew.bat equivalent under the jetbrains-gradle lease and label it as such.
definitionOfDone: A dispatcher test feeds raw ERROR frames to MoeMessageDispatcher. The new listener method receives the exact operation, codeName and context.taskId. A missing or non-string codeName or taskId arrives as null. Existing onError(operation, message) delivery is unchanged.

Named PlanReviewApprovalStateTest cases: a PENDING approval stays PENDING after an ERROR for another operation, after one for another task, and after one with no context. A later WORKING at the captured revision then reaches FINISHED.

Named tests: a correlated PLAN_REVISION_MISMATCH while PENDING ends INVALIDATED with PLAN_CHANGED_KEY and never re-arms. Any other correlated codeName (including none) re-arms READY with DAEMON_ERROR_KEY.
Fresh `cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test` exits 0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: JetBrains only: no daemon, wire-shape or moe-vscode changes; existing onError(operation, message) implementers keep compiling and behaving unchanged.

implementationPlan.description:
TESTS FIRST (RED). Load test-driven-development. CQ-I06a, a dependency, has landed onConnectionLost in the same three toolwindow files. Build on its landed bytes and never revert them.

1. NEW moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/services/MoeMessageDispatcherErrorTest.kt. Copy the harness from MoeMessageDispatcherAccountsTest: a Proxy fakeProject(), `MoeMessageDispatcher(project=fakeProject(), invokeLater={ it() }, isDisposed={ false }, currentState={ state }, updateState={ state = it }, onProjectMismatch={}, onDaemonShuttingDown={})`, and a listener that records BOTH onError(operation, message) and the new onDaemonError(DaemonError). Feed raw JSON through dispatcher.handle(...):
   - E1: the full refusal frame `{"type":"ERROR","message":"Plan changed","operation":"APPROVE_TASK","code":-32010,"codeName":"PLAN_REVISION_MISMATCH","context":{"taskId":"task-1","epicId":"epic-1","expectedPlanRevision":4,"currentPlanRevision":5}}`. Expect DaemonError("APPROVE_TASK", "PLAN_REVISION_MISMATCH", "task-1", "Plan changed") exactly, and onError("APPROVE_TASK", "Plan changed") exactly as today.
   - E2: the legacy frame `{"type":"ERROR","message":"Missing payload"}`. Expect DaemonError(null, null, null, "Missing payload"), with onError("unknown", "Missing payload") unchanged.
   - E3: hostile types, each giving the null field and never throwing:
     - codeName 7, true, null, {} and [];
     - context "task-1", [] and null;
     - context {"taskId":5}, {"taskId":null} and {"taskId":{}}.
     onError delivery stays as today for every frame whose operation and message are strings.
2. moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/PlanReviewApprovalStateTest.kt:
   - Migrate every existing `state.onDaemonError("APPROVE_TASK", "<text>")` call to `state.onDaemonError("APPROVE_TASK", taskId, null)`, a correlated error with no code. Their asserted semantics do not change. The step note must say this is a mechanical signature migration, not a weakening.
   - Add a section '// ---- daemon error correlation (CQ-I06d)', using the existing helpers (pendingAt, working, rendered, snapshot):
     - D1 `an error for another operation leaves a pending approval pending`. onDaemonError("UPDATE_SETTINGS", taskId, null) and onDaemonError("UPDATE_TASK", taskId, "PLAN_REVISION_MISMATCH") both return false, and the state stays PENDING. Then onStateUpdate(working(4L)) reaches FINISHED.
     - D2 `an error for another task leaves a pending approval pending`. onDaemonError("APPROVE_TASK", "task-other", "PLAN_REVISION_MISMATCH") returns false. Then working(4L) reaches FINISHED.
     - D3 `an error without context leaves a pending approval pending`. Both (null, null, null) and ("APPROVE_TASK", null, null) return false. Then working(4L) reaches FINISHED.
     - D4 `a correlated PLAN_REVISION_MISMATCH latches as plan changed`. It returns true and gives INVALIDATED, PLAN_CHANGED_KEY, approveEnabled false, captured 4L. onApproveClicked returns Blocked(PLAN_CHANGED_KEY). A later working(4L) leaves it INVALIDATED, never FINISHED.
     - D5 `any other correlated code re-arms with the daemon error notice`. Use a table over codeName null, "INVALID_INPUT", "TASK_NOT_FOUND" and "plan_revision_mismatch"; matching is exact and case-sensitive only. Each returns true and gives READY, DAEMON_ERROR_KEY, approveEnabled true. The next click sends Send(taskId, 4L).
     - D6 `a correlated error outside pending changes nothing`. In READY, INVALIDATED, FINISHED and DISPOSED, a correlated mismatch returns false and leaves the phase and notice unchanged.
     - D7, a source pin via dialogSource(): `the dialog routes only correlated daemon errors into the machine`. The source contains `override fun onDaemonError(error: DaemonError)` with `approval.onDaemonError(error.operation, error.taskId, error.codeName)` and `applyApprovalState()`, and no longer contains `approval.onDaemonError(operation, message)`.
RED: the test sources fail to compile, because DaemonError and the new signatures do not exist yet. Record that in the step note. Run the focused classes under the jetbrains-gradle lease: `cmd.exe /d /c "set GRADLE_OPTS=-Xmx512m&& cd /d <tree>\moe-jetbrains && .\gradlew.bat test --tests com.moe.toolwindow.PlanReviewApprovalStateTest --tests com.moe.services.MoeMessageDispatcherErrorTest"`.

VERIFY ONCE. Edit only what this step's findings need, and report it in modifiedFiles.

Run it fresh, under the `jetbrains-gradle` lease, and release the lease even on failure: `cmd.exe /d /c "set GRADLE_OPTS=-Xmx512m&& cd /d <tree>\moe-jetbrains && .\gradlew.bat test --rerun"`. 4. Give complete_task the gate command, labelled as the Windows equivalent, with its exit code and the output tail.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, once, last. Load adversarial-self-review. Read the diff as someone trying to make JetBrains report an approval wrongly, or drift from VS Code. Check:
- Ordering: the newer-revision frame arriving BEFORE the correlated PLAN_REVISION_MISMATCH. It already latched, so the error is a no-op. Also a mismatch followed by WORKING at the captured revision.
- A board-originated APPROVE_TASK refusal for the same task while the dialog is pending. It correlates by task id, exactly as VS Code does; note that this is intended.
- Thread safety: dispatcher invokeLater, then the machine lock, then an EDT-only repaint.
- Hostile frames: huge message text (still bounded by MAX_ERROR_CHARS), non-string fields, a context array, a missing operation.
- The four other onError listeners are unaffected: status bar, tool window, metrics, and the dialog's former route. The tool window's error notification still fires.
- Strings match exactly: no trimming and no case folding.
- Rails: JetBrains only, with no daemon, wire or moe-vscode edits; no .moe edits; no Git writes; none of globalRails.forbiddenPatterns.
Then write the Serena memory 'task-task-6dbeb9712cda46488b80ce23afe35198-handoff' for CQ-I06b. Record:
- the corpus mapping: an error event is (operation, taskId, codeName). The machine's verdicts are: ignored leaves it unchanged, a correlated mismatch latches, any other correlated error re-arms;
- the new DaemonError listener API.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Change onError(operation, message) to carry the new fields. Rejected: it would break four implementers (MoeStatusBarWidget, MoeToolWindowPanel, MetricsPanel, PlanReviewDialog). A default onDaemonError(DaemonError) method is added instead.
- Filter only by operation in the dialog. Rejected: an APPROVE_TASK error for another task, for example a board approval, would still re-arm, and VS Code correlates by context.taskId.
- Put the correlation in the dialog. Rejected: the dialog cannot be tested headlessly. The machine already knows its taskId and holds the lock, so correlation lives there and D1-D6 test it directly.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- MoeMessageDispatcher.kt, "ERROR" branch (about line 180): it reads only message and operation, via safeAsString. safeAsString calls asString, which throws on an object or array. Neither codeName nor context is parsed.
- Daemon WebSocketServer error frame (around line 1145): {type:'ERROR', message, operation: message.type, code?, codeName? (MoeError only), context: {taskId, epicId, expectedPlanRevision?, currentPlanRevision?} (only when a payload exists)}. It is sent to the requesting socket only. Envelope and payload errors carry no operation or context.
- MoeStateListener.onError has a default no-op. Implementers: MoeStatusBarWidget:44, MoeToolWindowPanel:347 (shows a notification), MetricsPanel:146, PlanReviewDialog.
- Existing test call sites: PlanReviewApprovalStateTest calls onDaemonError("APPROVE_TASK", text) six times. Migrate them to ("APPROVE_TASK", taskId, null).
- MoeMessageDispatcherAccountsTest holds the dispatcher harness: a Proxy fakeProject and a synchronous invokeLater.
- VS Code reference, PlanReviewPanel.handleClientError: it requires operation === 'APPROVE_TASK' and context.taskId === this.taskId, and treats the error as stale when codeName === 'PLAN_REVISION_MISMATCH'.
planningNotes.risks:
- CQ-I06a edits the same three toolwindow files. This task dependsOn it, so build on its landed bytes and never revert onConnectionLost.
- Six distinct files is one over the size warning: four small production edits and two test files, about 190 net LOC. The daemon floors the plan to the heavy tier, which allows Opus only.
- If the shared tree is mid-merge, gate in a snapshot.
- The Kotlin compiler here rejects `arrayOf(stringValue, intValue)`. Use arrayOf<Any> or typed lists in tables.
